prompt.context: Massive Dynamic is a multi-national pharmaceutical company. One of their assets, Cortexiphan, is an anti-infective that successfully treats three major types of hospital-born illness and is currently in Phase II clinical trials. Unfortunately, Massive Dynamic only has the capital to finance a Phase III clinical trial for one of the three illnesses that Cortexiphan treats.
prompt.question: Walter Bishop, Chief Medical Officer of Massive Dynamic, has enlisted your help to decide which of the three possible indications for Cortexiphan they should pursue to maximize profits over a five-year period post-launch.

clarifying_info.a: The drug is only likely to be approved in the US at this time.

clarifying_info.q: How will the drug be distributed/sold?
clarifying_info.a: The drug will be sold directly to hospitals by Massive Dynamic; no need to consider distribution channel costs.

clarifying_info.q: Should we use NPV or total undiscounted cash flows?
clarifying_info.a: No need to calculate based on NPV; just do total over five years without discounting.

exhibits.title: Market Overview by Indication
exhibits.shows: A table showing three indications (Candidiasis, Rare Molds, Aspergillosis) with the number of competitors (6, 2, 4), their individual market shares, annual dose volumes, and average price per dose.

exhibits.title: Clinical and Development Profile by Indication
exhibits.shows: A table comparing the three indications on Phase III trial success probability, Phase III trial cost, production cost per dose, safety profile vs. market leader, and efficacy profile vs. market leader.

exhibits.title: Cortexiphan Aspergillosis Formulary Status Distribution by Pricing Strategy
exhibits.shows: A table showing how different pricing strategies (Discount $5, Parity $10, Premium $15) affect the distribution of hospitals across formulary statuses (No Restrictions, On Formulary Restricted, Off Formulary) and the expected market share at each formulary status.

framework: Define the objective: maximize 5-year post-launch profits across three indications
Assess market attractiveness for each indication: total market size, competitive dynamics, and market share potential given clinical profile
Estimate annual profitability per indication: (price - production cost) x (market share x annual doses)
Incorporate development risk and cost: expected profit = (P_success x 5-year profit) - (P_fail x trial cost)
Evaluate pricing strategy (premium vs. parity vs. discount) for the chosen indication using formulary status impact on market share
Confirm final recommendation with risk discussion

questions.prompt: What are your initial thoughts on the three indications based on Exhibit 1? Calculate the total market size for each.
questions.guidance: Candidate should note: Aspergillosis has 4 competitors with two sparingly used, signaling room for a strong entrant. Rare Molds has only 2 competitors with one clear leader; physicians likely want alternatives and a lower-cost option than $20 could be attractive if economics work. Candidiasis is very crowded with 6 competitors and no clear leader; strong clinical differentiation required to penetrate. Candidate should also calculate total market size for each indication.

math.setup: Total market size = Annual Doses x Avg Price per Dose
math.answer: Candidiasis is the largest market ($25B), followed by Aspergillosis ($15B) and Rare Molds ($4B). However, market size alone is insufficient; development costs and likely market share must be evaluated.

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 2, estimate Cortexiphan's likely market share in each indication and calculate annual profits.
questions.guidance: Candidate should reason about market share from the clinical profile: Aspergillosis - superior efficacy makes Cortexiphan the likely new market leader (~50-60%). Rare Molds - equal clinical profile; likely to split the market with the current leader, slightly below given first-mover disadvantage (~40-50%). Candidiasis - poor safety profile in a crowded market at the same price; unlikely to be a significant player (much less than 25%). After discussion, use: Asp=60%, Rare Molds=40%, Candidiasis=10%. Then calculate annual profit.

math.setup: Annual Profit = (Price per Dose - Production Cost per Dose) x (Market Share x Annual Doses)
math.answer: Aspergillosis generates the highest annual profit at $2.7B, followed by Candidiasis ($1.5B) and Rare Molds ($1.2B).

questions.prompt: Incorporate the probability of trial success and trial cost to calculate the expected 5-year profit for each indication.
questions.guidance: Candidate should use expected value: Expected Profit = (P_success x 5-year profit if success) - (P_fail x trial cost). Five-year profit if success = Annual Profit x 5 minus trial cost. The candidate should drive to the conclusion that Aspergillosis has the highest expected profit and is the recommended indication.

math.setup: Expected Profit = (P_success x [Annual Profit x 5 - Trial Cost]) - (P_fail x Trial Cost). Equivalently: (P_success x 5yr gross profit) - Trial Cost
steps: Aspergillosis 5yr profit if success: $2.7B x 5 - $2B = $13.5B - $2B = $11.5B; Expected: 50% x $11.5B - 50% x $2B = $5.75B - $1B = $4.75B
Rare Molds 5yr profit if success: $1.2B x 5 - $0.5B = $6B - $0.5B = $5.5B; Expected: 25% x $5.5B - 75% x $0.5B = $1.375B - $0.375B = $1.0B
Candidiasis 5yr profit if success: $1.5B x 5 - $1B = $7.5B - $1B = $6.5B; Expected: 60% x $6.5B - 40% x $1B = $3.9B - $0.4B = $3.5B
math.answer: Aspergillosis: $4.75B expected profit. Candidiasis: $3.5B. Rare Molds: $1.0B. Aspergillosis is the preferred indication.

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 3, calculate the effective market share and annual revenue for Cortexiphan in Aspergillosis at each price point (Discount $5, Parity $10, Premium $15). Which pricing strategy maximizes profit?
questions.guidance: Candidate should recognize qualitatively that higher price leads to worse formulary status and lower market share. They should calculate overall effective market share as a sum-product of (% hospitals at each formulary status) x (expected market share at that status), then compute revenue and profit.

math.setup: Effective Market Share = sum over statuses of [% Hospitals in Status x Expected Market Share in Status]. Annual Revenue = 1.5B doses x Effective Market Share x Price. Annual Profit = (Price - $7 cost) x 1.5B x Effective Market Share. 5-year profit = Annual Profit x 5 - $2B trial cost.
steps: Premium 5-year profit: ($15 - $7) x 0.75B doses/yr x 5 yrs - $2B trial = $8 x 0.75B x 5 - $2B = $30B - $2B = $28B
math.answer: Premium pricing ($15/dose) yields the highest revenue ($11.25B/yr) and 5-year profit ($28B net of trial cost). Profit increases with price despite lower market share because higher margin more than compensates.

brainstorming.prompt: Dr. Bishop agrees with the aspergillosis indication. He is wondering whether pricing at either a discount or premium to the market will result in increased profitability. What are the main pros and cons of each strategy?

categories.name: Premium Pricing - Pros
ideas: Signals to market that the product is clinically superior, matching the actual efficacy profile
Allows selective discounts to specific hospitals without proactively sacrificing revenue

categories.name: Premium Pricing - Cons
ideas: Lower formulary status and market share
Bad publicity given current media and government pressure on high-priced pharmaceuticals
May limit pricing flexibility for other indications (Rare Molds, Candidiasis) pursued later

categories.name: Discount Pricing - Pros
ideas: Higher market share and quicker product uptake
Builds volume and physician familiarity with the drug
Can take price increases over time once established

categories.name: Discount Pricing - Cons
ideas: Sets a low price anchor that could hinder pricing potential for other indications if pursued later
May signal lower quality despite superior clinical profile

recommendation: Pursue the Aspergillosis indication at a premium price of $15 per dose
This strategy yields an expected 5-year profit of approximately $28B (net of $2B trial cost) and total expected revenue of $56.25B over five years
risks: There is a 50% probability that the Phase III trial fails, resulting in a $2B loss
Premium pricing will lead to worse formulary status and lower market share (~50%) compared to discount pricing (~66%)
Government and media scrutiny of high pharmaceutical pricing could create reputational and regulatory risk
If the aspergillosis trial fails, Massive Dynamic loses the $2B investment with no revenue
next_steps: Initiate Phase III clinical trial for Aspergillosis indication immediately given capital constraints
Develop a hospital relations and formulary strategy to maximize placement despite premium pricing
Monitor competitive dynamics and be prepared to adjust pricing if new entrants emerge
Evaluate potential to pursue Rare Molds or Candidiasis indications in subsequent funding rounds
